sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash live preview — Gemini API
sources.evidence: Exact endpoint documentation, updated October 19, 2026: legacy preview; 131,072 input and 65,536 output tokens; text/audio output; thinking and function calling supported. Its input summary omits video, but its migration section still documents video-frame handling. Function calling is synchronous.

sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash with Native Audio Capabilities (Flash Live) Model Card — March 2026
sources.evidence: The original exact-model card lists text, image, video and audio input; text and audio output; 128K context. It explicitly refers architecture and training details to the Gemini 3 Pro model card. Distribution is through hosted Google services and APIs; no model parameter count is given.

sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash Audio (Flash Live, TTS) Model Card — April 2026 update
sources.evidence: Updated card retains separate Live specifications: four input modalities, text/audio output and 128K context. It directs the architecture to Gemini 3 Pro, describes hosted API distribution under service terms, and supplies no total or active parameter count.

sources.title: Gemini 3 Pro Model Card — May 2026 update
sources.evidence: This is the architecture reference explicitly designated by the Live model cards. It describes a sparse mixture-of-experts Transformer and lists Gemini 3.1 Flash Live among derived family members. It does not state the Live variant's total or active parameter counts.

sources.title: Build real-time conversational agents with Gemini 3.1 Flash Live
sources.evidence: March 26, 2026 launch announcement by Google DeepMind staff explicitly announces preview availability through the Gemini Live API and uses the exact gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview identifier.

sources.title: Gemini API release notes
sources.evidence: The March 26, 2026 entry explicitly records release of gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview for real-time dialogue and voice applications.

sources.title: Gemini API Additional Terms of Service
sources.evidence: The service terms govern Gemini API use and prohibit extraction or replication of underlying models, including parameter weights. Along with the card's hosted distribution, this supports a proprietary classification rather than an open-weight license.

sources.title: Gemini 3.8 Audio Model Card — September 2026
sources.evidence: Checked this later audio-family card for exact predecessor disclosures. It supplies no Gemini 3.1 Flash Live total or active parameter count. Its newer-model capabilities were not transferred to this record.

sources.title: Gemini Audio — Live dialogue
sources.evidence: The current comparison page names Gemini 3.1 Flash Live in comparisons against Gemini 3.8 Live, including High and Minimal reasoning variants. It supplies performance comparisons, not parameter counts.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon Model Card — October 2026
sources.evidence: Checked the later flagship card for retrospective exact-model size disclosures; no Gemini 3.1 Flash Live total or active parameter count is supplied.

sources.title: Gemini deprecations
sources.evidence: The current table schedules this endpoint's shutdown for November 17, 2026 and names Gemini 3.8 Live as its replacement. Its March 11 release date conflicts with the explicit March 26 release-note entry and launch announcement.

name.note: Official name and exact preview endpoint match.

developer.note: Google DeepMind developed the model; Google is the catalog's developer grouping.

family.note: Flash-branded Gemini model; retain the catalog's Gemini Flash family key.

release_date.note: Retain the explicit public launch date corroborated by the exact-endpoint changelog. The deprecations table instead says March 11; no contemporaneous public release evidence for that earlier date was found.

open_weights.note: Hosted model under API service terms; the documented distribution provides no downloadable checkpoint.

license.note: Descriptive classification for the Google-hosted model under Gemini API terms, not the documentation's separate content license.

parameters_b.note: No exact Live total was disclosed in the reviewed original/updated cards or later comparisons. Targeted first-party training and interpretability searches found no additional count. Also checked later 3.5, 3.7 and 3.8 Flash cards; no sibling size was transferred.

active_parameters_b.note: Sparse expert routing does not disclose a numeric active count; the reviewed sources provide none for this Live variant.

architecture.note: The exact Live cards explicitly designate Gemini 3 Pro as their architecture reference; that card specifies a sparse MoE Transformer. This is an explicit reference chain, not an inference from the Flash name.

context_window.note: Exact endpoint input-token limit; the separate output limit is 65,536.

modalities.note: Exact original and updated Live cards explicitly include video input and both output types. The current API summary row omits video, but its video-frame instructions remain; record this documentation inconsistency without discarding explicit capability evidence.

reasoning.note: Thinking is supported with configurable levels.

tool_call.note: Function calling is supported, with synchronous execution only.

description.value: Preview Live API model for real-time voice and video dialogue, with text and audio responses, configurable thinking, and synchronous function calling.

patch.notes: Sparse MoE Transformer architecture is established by the exact model card's explicit reference to Gemini 3 Pro; total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed. Exact Live specifications retain 131,072 input tokens and text/audio outputs. The current API input summary omits video, while both model cards and API migration instructions support it. March 26, 2026 is the explicit public launch and changelog date; the deprecations table inconsistently lists March 11. As of this audit, Google schedules shutdown for November 17, 2026; endpoint operation was not tested.

summary: Add verified MoE architecture and proprietary classification, replace the qualitative description, and upgrade provenance to first-party sources. Retain the exact Live endpoint's context, modalities, reasoning and tool support. Counts remain null after original, updated and later-card checks. Preserve the corroborated March 26 public release date while recording the contradictory deprecation-table date and video-summary omission.
